title: Gorillaz Return to Mexico City, Praising Its 'Revolutionary Spirit'
summary: Gorillaz are back in Mexico City. On Friday, November 20, the British band headlined the first day of the Corona Capital festival, returning to the city for the first time in eight years. About 72,000 people packed the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, according to promoter Ocesa. Lead singer Damon Albarn praised Mexico's 'revolutionary spirit' from the stage. He also praised Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, who had flown in economy class to a meeting in Shenzhen, China, the week before. Albarn called the choice an important statement, and he saluted the crowd. Albarn wore a red beret and a military-style jacket on Mexico's Revolution Day, marked every November 20 for the start of the 1910 uprising against Porfirio Díaz, who had ruled for more than 30 years. The show was full of special guests. Guitarist Johnny Marr joined for songs from Gorillaz's 2026 album The Mountain. Argentine rapper Trueno joined for 'THE MANIFESTO' and freestyled during 'Clint Eastwood,' the song that closed the show. Mexican singer Luisa Almaguer joined for 'Latin Simone (¿Qué Pasa Contigo?).' Kara Jackson, Bootie Brown, and Black Thought also took the stage.
why_it_matters: It shows how music can bring huge crowds together and celebrate a country's history.
